content:
aisha: Heads-up — noticed a batch of negative invoice adjustments for a handful of tenants after the route-metadata deploy earlier. Looks correlated with route_tag schema flip.

dan: ugh. can you paste an example tenant id / event chain?

aisha: tenant: t-4932. here are two adjacent events from the ingest stream (redacted):
```
{"event_id":"e-1001","route_tags":{"tier":"pro","discount_tag":null},"tokens":120}
{"event_id":"e-1002","route_tags":null,"tokens":80}
```
Second one lost the tags during enrichment, ratecard applied as default free-tier -> invoice delta.

kevin: hmm that smells like the epoch shim we added for route_tag_v2. If enrich reads old key name and falls back to null, downstream aggregator treats it as a different bucket.

belinda: We also saw the console preview showing token tallies that don't match the ledger. Preview pipeline uses the canonicalized tag, ledger uses the enriched attribute — mismatch window when both v1 and v2 coexist.

dan: how many events impacted overall? rough numbers ok.

metering-bot: detected 1,432 events in last 3h with missing route_tags after enrichment. 87 unique tenants affected. (alert suppressed)

kevin: ok that's enough to call it an incident for accounting. short-term mitigation: should we add a compatibility layer in the aggregator that treats null tag as "fallback-to-prev-seen" until backfill completes?

aisha: proposal: 1) add aggregator compatibility to map null -> last_known_tag for tenant-session for 12h 2) trigger a backfill job to reprocess enrichment for the 3h window 3) add an alert for tag-drop rate > 0.1% per tenant

belinda: agree. also add a dashboard card in Console showing tag-propagation success rate per route and per region — makes this visible to customers too.

kevin: implementation note: last_known_tag mapping requires tenant-session binding; we already record last_route_tag in session-state but it's optional. We can make aggregator consult session-state cache before applying default.

dan: is there any chance double-charging could happen with the fix? e.g., reprocess + live mapping causing duplicates in ledger.

aisha: good call — reprocess should write events to a replay topic with idempotency keys set to original event_id so ledger consumer dedupes. aggregator compatibility does not emit new ledger writes, it only influences preview and downstream scoring until backfill finishes.

metering-bot: replay topic created: metering.replay. Pending 1,432 events. 0 consumers attached.

dan: can someone own the backfill run? need runbook steps.

belinda: i can run backfill with ops help. steps: attach consumer to replay, enable idempotent writes flag on ledger producer, dry-run on dev cluster first.

kevin: estimated churn: 10-15m to wire compatibility layer, 30-45m to run backfill (depends on throughput). I can pair with belinda on the deploy.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of aggregator-compat v1 started at 1764567910, canary on 2 pods in us-west.

aisha: thanks. after canary, we'll watch two things: preview vs ledger token divergence and ratecard assignment histogram. if divergence > 1% stop and rollback.

belinda: will add a temporary console alert: preview_ledger_delta_pct > 1% for any tenant.

dan: postmortem item: we need a contract test that guarantees route_tag presence/compatibility across enrich/aggregator + a telemetry contract that surfaces propagation latency.

kevin: agree. also consider making enrichment emit a tag-propagation metric (0/1 per event) with tags: route_version, region.

aisha: filed follow-ups: GH-#1829 (aggregator compatibility), GH-#1830 (backfill runbook), GH-#1831 (console alert & dashboard card), GH-#1832 (enrichment metric). tagging owners accordingly.

belinda: i'll coordinate the backfill with support so affected tenants get a heads-up in case invoice previews change.

dan: thanks team. keep updates here.
